validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE confirmed independent of GEM/wiki: this is FERC Docket No. CP20-16-000, 'Westbrook XPress Project,' filed by Portland Natural Gas Transmission System (PNGTS) on Nov 18, 2019 (Federal Register 2019-26339), requesting authorization to construct Phases II and III of the project (an additional 15,900 hp compressor unit + modifications at the Westbrook Compressor Station and Westbrook Metering & Regulating Station, all in Cumberland County, Maine). Independently confirmed in the EIA 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical workbook as 'Westbrook Xpress Project Phase 2,' Docket CP20-16, Capacity 63 MMcf/d, Completed/In-Service 2021 -- an exact match to the sheet's recorded Capacity (63.00) and StartYear1/ConstructionYear (2021). CLASSIFICATION correct: a legitimate FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas compression capacity-expansion project, correctly carrying LengthKnown=0/blank Diameter per the compression-only-expansion convention (the only new pipe described in the FERC filing is ~1,500 ft of 30-inch suction/discharge line confined within the existing compressor station site, not a new mapped route). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row US-gas roster and the sibling PNGTS cluster: distinct from P0242 (the PNGTS mainline itself, Pittsburg NH-Westbrook ME, 1999, 210 MMcf/d), P2588 ('Portland Xpress Expansion Project', an earlier, separate FERC docket family -- CP18-251/CP18-479/CP18-506 -- completed 2018-2020, ~24 MMcf/d), and P3280 (this project's own sibling 'Phase 3', same CP20-16 docket, 18 MMcf/d, completed 2021). EIA independently tracks Phase 2 (63 MMcf/d) and Phase 3 (18 MMcf/d) as separate line items that sum to the FERC filing's stated combined 80,998 Mcf/d (~81 MMcf/d) wholly-owned-system capacity increase -- confirming GEM's phase-level row split is correct, not double-counted.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndState/Province=Quebec / EndCountryOrArea=Canada for this row does not match where the project's facilities physically are. The Nov 18, 2019 FERC Notice of Application (2019-26339) and the Dec 19, 2019 Notice of Intent to Prepare an EA (2019-27320) both state, in near-identical language, that ALL of the Westbrook XPress Project's new/modified facilities -- the new compressor unit, the ~1,500 ft of 30-inch suction/discharge line, and the Westbrook Metering & Regulating Station modifications -- are 'located in Cumberland County, Maine.' This is corroborated independently by the EIA 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook, which records Beg_State=QU (Quebec, i.e. upstream of the border interconnect) but End_State=ME for BOTH this row ('Phase 2') and its sibling 'Phase 3' (P3280) -- and P3280 in fact already carries the correct EndState/Province=Maine on the live sheet, making P2631's Quebec end-state an isolated inconsistency within its own project family, not a considered scope difference. A Quebec endpoint would also be facially inconsistent with this being a US FERC-jurisdictional Natural Gas Act section 7(c) certificate proceeding for compressor-station work sited entirely in Maine. StartState/Province=New Hampshire/United States is left unchanged -- it correctly reflects PNGTS's upstream interconnect with TransCanada PipeLines Limited at Pittsburg, NH (the same convention used for the P0242 mainline row and the P3280 sibling row), even though this specific phase's physical construction work is concentrated at the Maine end.

(a subsidiary of Energir L.P.) agreed March 4, 2024 to sell 100% of PNGTS to BlackRock (through a fund managed by its Diversified Infrastructure business) and investment funds managed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners, gross purchase price US$1.14 billion (including US$250 million of assumed Senior Notes); the sale closed August 15, 2024, and PNGTS became a standalone company (CEO Bill Yardley). validity.researcher_notes: The only project-cost figure found, '$117.3 million,' appears in the Nov 18, 2019 FERC Notice of Application (2019-26339) as the applicant's own estimate for 'the project' -- explicitly defined earlier in the same sentence as 'Westbrook XPress Project Phases II and III' together, i.e. this row (Phase 2/P2631) AND its sibling P3280 (Phase 3) combined. The EIA workbook happens to list this same $117.3M figure entirely under its 'Phase 2' line item while leaving 'Phase 3''s Cost field blank -- almost certainly an EIA data-entry convention (attributing a joint-docket cost to the first-listed phase) rather than evidence the full amount belongs to Phase 2 alone. Per the project's aggregate-vs-segment rule, a combined/system figure is never a valid ref for one segment's cost cell. Recommend leaving SegmentCost UNRESOLVED for both P2631 and P3280 rather than assigning the full $117.3M (or an unsourced arbitrary split) to either row alone; flagged as a cross_row_lead to P3280 below.

The FERC EA-intent notice (2019-27320) does state a pipe diameter -- 30-inch -- for the project's suction/discharge lines, but that pipe is an approximately 1,500-foot in-station jumper connecting a new compressor to the existing station, not a mapped route-level pipeline segment; per the LengthKnown=0/blank-Diameter convention for compression-only capacity expansions with no new mapped route pipe, filling Diameter=30 here would misrepresent an in-station fitting as the segment's pipe diameter. Leaving Diameter blank/UNRESOLVED is the correct recorded state, consistent with the companion Length fill above and with how P0242 (the mainline row) and its own Diameter field are handled.

summary: P2631 (PNGTS Westbrook Xpress Project Phase 2, FERC Docket CP20-16-000) is confirmed as a real, correctly-classified, currently-operating compression-only capacity-expansion project, not a duplicate of P0242/P2588/P3280 -- EIA's independently-compiled dataset gives an exact Capacity match (63 MMcf/d) and confirms the phase-level split against sibling P3280 (18 MMcf/d) sums to the FERC filing's combined 80,998 Mcf/d increase. Staged REFS_ADDED on 10 of 15 worklist units: Status, Fuel, Proposal (2019-11, single-source), Construction (2021), Start (refined to 2021-11 via the FERC commencement filing), Capacity, Length (confirms LengthKnown=0 is correct per the compression-only-expansion convention), FuelSource (Marcellus/Utica supply basins, single-source), and -- the two most consequential findings -- Location and Owner/Operator. LOCATION: corrected EndState/Province and EndCountryOrArea from Quebec/Canada to Maine/United States -- all project facilities are confirmed in Cumberland County, Maine by two independent government/dataset sources; this was an isolated inconsistency within the row's own project family (sibling P3280 already carries the correct Maine end-state). OWNERSHIP: TC Energy (61.7%)/Northern New England Investment Co. (38.3%) sold PNGTS to BlackRock (Diversified Infrastructure business) + Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners, closing Aug 15, 2024 (sheet's LastUpdated=2023-08-03 predates this); Operator newly populated as PNGTS itself, now a standalone company. A spec concern is flagged without an invented fix: SegmentCost's only found figure ($117.3M) is an explicit combined Phase II+III estimate, not separable to this row alone (aggregate-vs-segment rule) -- left UNRESOLVED and cross-referenced to P3280. UNRESOLVED (4 units): Delay (no evidence of an actual delay found; DelayType=inferred requires no citation), Pressure (no MAOP figure found in any FERC notice reviewed), Diameter (the only diameter found, 30-inch, describes a short in-station jumper, not a mapped route segment -- blank is the correct state per convention), and SegmentCost. Two cross_row_leads staged: P3280 (the shared $117.3M cost ambiguity) and P2588 (a likely EIA 'Portland Xpress Project Phase 3' correspondence with a close-but-inexact capacity match, 24.375 vs the sheet's 24.00, plus the same flagged Quebec-endpoint pattern -- not independently verified this session, routed for direct research).
